state.k2_horizon_provenance: CORRECTED, and the correction matters. ROADMAP 9.15 said k2_horizon 'has no upstream oracle because llama.cpp dropped the architecture', which implies the architecture existed and its implementation is recoverable. It never did: absent from src/llama-arch.{h,cpp} at 3653e6d, and a GitHub search of the ENTIRE upstream issue+PR tracker for 'k2_horizon' returns 0 results in any state (the local clone is depth-1, so git history could not be searched and the API search is what settles it; 'kimi_k2' by contrast returns 6, the newest being open PR #26757 'model: Add support for A.X K2'). So there is nothing to recover and nothing to arbitrate against. The honest options for that forward pass are a fixture plus an oracle we write ourselves -- which is not independent -- or a structural oracle that does not need to know the architecture at all. One candidate, worked out but NOT built: GQA group-permutation equivariance. Permute the KV heads of attn_k/attn_v and the query heads of attn_q/attn_output consistently at group granularity and the logits must be bit-identical under h/n_rep and NOT under h%n_kv, provided n_kv neither divides nor equals n_rep (n_head_kv == 2 is a coincidence, which is why the existing fixtures cannot see it). It needs a k2_horizon fixture plus a tensor-permuting GGUF rewriter; scripts/gguf_patch_kv.py only rewrites string metadata keys today.

state.ggml_dot_port: src/ggml_dot.rs: ggml_dot_f32 (the kernel, wired into Model::matvec) and ggml_rms_norm_scale (wired into rmsnorm), pinned by tests/data/dot_golden.bin -- 243 dot products the kernel actually computed, across 35 lengths, operands included -- and tests/dot_golden.rs, 243/243 bit-identical. A real model never reaches it -- a matvec's ne0 is n_embd or n_ff, always a multiple of 32 -- which is why only gemma3's toy widths (48,56,70) exposed it.

state.rms_norm_is_the_other_rule: ggml_compute_forward_rms_norm_f32 (ops.cpp:3828) is NOT vec_dot: a hand-written loop with a ggml_float -- a DOUBLE -- accumulator over f32-rounded products, then mean = sum/ne00 narrowed to f32 and scale = 1.0f/sqrtf(mean+eps). The engine's rmsnorm was doing sum::<f32>(). So the mat-mul and the norm use DIFFERENT reduction rules in the same transformer, and a blanket 'accumulate in f64' is wrong for one of them while a blanket 'use the SIMD tree' is wrong for the other. Neither mistake is visible in an accuracy metric; both are simply 'close'.
state.f32_residual_open: THE 4.07e-06 IS NOW UNEXPLAINED, and that is the open question rather than a gap in coverage. Every op the budget measured is at round-off, and the one that was not (rope, 2.1e-4) turned out not to reach the logits at all. So the next move is NOT another op sweep. It is a PER-LAYER DIVERGENCE TRACE: run both sides and measure the relative L2 of the residual stream at each of the 36 layer outputs, which says whether the error is injected evenly (f32 rounding, irreducible) or amplified somewhere (a small per-call error that compounds). state.layernorm_reduction: DONE, and it refuted the reason it was open. src/model.rs:1189 claimed the reference reduces layernorm's mean and variance in `double` 'because ggml_vec_norm_f32 and ggml_vec_rmsnorm_f32 both accumulate into a ggml_float'. Both halves are FALSE at 3653e6d: ggml_vec_rmsnorm_f32 no longer exists (RMSNorm is a hand-written loop in ops.cpp:3828, already ported as ggml_rms_norm_scale), and ggml_vec_norm_f32 (vec.h:858) is a one-line call to ggml_vec_dot_f32 -- it is the dot kernel, and LayerNorm does not call it. What ggml_compute_forward_norm_f32 (ops.cpp:3698) calls is TWO reductions with TWO shapes: ggml_vec_sum_f32 (vec.h:1495) for the mean, a plain sequential ggml_float accumulator narrowed then divided IN F32; and ggml_vec_cvar_f32 (vec.cpp:455) for the variance, a ggml_float accumulator fed ONE f32 per group of 8 by a horizontal tree, with the division in double. So the blanket rule the note recommended is right for the mean and wrong for the variance inside one function, which is why eight ticks of 'accumulate in f64' reasoning never found it.

The budget OVERSHOOTS by 3 orders of magnitude because RoPE's error is a coherent ROTATION: every head and every layer gets the SAME angle error, so it cancels rather than accumulating. Tested rather than argued -- porting the largest per-op error to bit-exactness moved the end-to-end residual by NOTHING (4.07e-06 -> 4.55e-06 -> 4.07e-06, argmax 17/17). state.rope_is_f32_end_to_end: PORTED, bit-exact. ggml_compute_forward_rope_flt (ops.cpp:5953) + ggml_rope_cache_init (ops.cpp:5846) are f32 throughout: powf, the ladder, and sinf/cosf. Two details the source does not state: (1) the ladder must be CARRIED -- the reference keeps one f32 theta and multiplies it by theta_scale per pair, so theta_i is a chain of roundings and pos*cur with a separately accumulated cur diverges from the third pair; (2) both products CONTRACT into an FMA, because rotate_pairs is compiled into an -O3 .so and nothing in the source says so. key_finding_this_tick: A per-op error budget is the right instrument for the question it was built for and the WRONG instrument for the question tick 32 actually had. Built it, measured every op on the engine's own activations, and the composition step -- a random walk over independent roundings -- overshoots the measured end-to-end residual by three orders of magnitude. The reason is structural, not numerical: RoPE's error is a coherent rotation, and a coherent error applied identically at every head and every layer cancels instead of accumulating. So the budget was tested by porting its largest term: a 2.11e-4 per-op error made BIT-EXACT moved the logits by nothing. Two conclusions, and the second is the more useful one. (1) Every measured op is now at round-off against the reference and the 4.07e-06 residual is unexplained -- the next question is what it is made of, not which op is missing. (2) A per-op number does not compose into a per-model number, so any future 'fully explained' claim has to be checked against the end-to-end number, and here it disagreed by 3 orders of magnitude. The port itself is real: RoPE is f32 end to end in the reference, the engine was f64, the ladder has to be carried rather than recomputed, and both products have to contract into an FMA because that is only visible in the compiler's output.
next_steps: The 4.07e-06 is unexplained and that is the next question, not another op sweep. The decisive instrument is a PER-LAYER DIVERGENCE TRACE -- relative L2 of the residual stream at each of the 36 layer outputs, engine vs llama.cpp -- which distinguishes an error injected evenly (f32 rounding, irreducible) from one amplified somewhere (small per-call error that compounds). Every number this project has is at the logits, which is 36 layers of composition with no visibility inside.

Finish the elementwise port, now that it is bounded: the engine uses libm expf in SiLU and softmax where the reference uses the ggml_v_expf polynomial. Measured at 3.78e-08 and 7.01e-08 on real activations, so low-priority, and the softmax has two more differences to port (the 8-lane f32 tree into a double, and 1.0/sum in double rather than an f32 divide).

The budget's own lesson: a per-op number does not compose into a per-model number. Any 'fully explained' claim must be checked against the end-to-end number -- here it disagreed by 3 orders of magnitude -- and the overshoot is structure, not noise.
